title: Bi-Directional CRM Sync Out-of-Order Customer Data Rollback
businessContext: An enterprise SaaS platform syncs customer data bi-directionally with HubSpot and Salesforce. Sales reps noticed that customer email addresses and subscription tiers were mysteriously reverting to old values.
problemStatement: Because webhooks travel over asynchronous public internet networks, network delays can cause Event #2 (User upgraded to Enterprise at 10:05) to arrive BEFORE Event #1 (User updated profile email at 10:01). The sync handler blind-updates the database whenever an event arrives, causing the older Event #1 to overwrite newer data from Event #2. Implement monotonic versioning or Lamport timestamps to reject out-of-order writes.
constraints: Must guarantee stale older events can never overwrite newer state.
Must handle events arriving out-of-order or duplicate deliveries.
Update database only if `event.version > record.version` or `event.timestamp > record.updated_at`.
candidateTasks: Explain why network delivery order cannot be assumed in distributed webhooks.
Implement conditional SQL updates: `UPDATE customers SET ... WHERE id = $1 AND updated_at < $2`.
Explain how Distributed Tracing and event versioning prevent split-brain updates.
hints: Add a condition to the UPDATE query: `WHERE id = $1 AND updated_at < $eventTimestamp`.
If `rowCount === 0`, check if the row exists; if it exists with a higher timestamp, discard the event as a stale out-of-order event.
alternativeApproaches: Using an Event Sourcing model (Kafka / EventStore) with consumer partition ordering by CustomerId.
Vector Clocks / Lamport Timestamps across multiple distributed writing systems.
commonMistakes: Doing `SELECT updated_at` in JavaScript, checking `if (eventTime > dbTime)`, and then executing `UPDATE`: this creates a race condition between concurrent webhook workers.
Relying on server wall-clock arrival time instead of the event payload generation timestamp.
